case_note: Four cases are chosen by their known outcome to illustrate one pattern each. The fourth is the first correct live StartLux-9B answer that arrived after 1,000 ms in the first 80 requests/s repeat; its count is out of the successful live requests in that cell, where inputs repeat. The cases explain the comparison and are not a representative sample.

clinc_service.note: Four direct services on the 600 CLINC main-test inputs, five 180-second repeats per rate, 500 ms SLO from scheduled arrival. CPU services ran one inference thread; GPU services used a 0.40 memory share. Ranges are min-max across repeats. The test set had been scored before, so quality is retrospective.
clinc_service.title: CLINC · CPU classifier versus GPU services

cpu_baselines.note: CLINC banking intents with out-of-scope queries: 600 main-test inputs (450 banking, 150 out of scope); mixed is the 1,300-input stress workload with 65% out of scope. CPU classifiers were trained on 400 or 1,600 labelled examples and evaluated retrospectively; LLM rows are the frozen V1 predictions.
cpu_baselines.title: CLINC · cheap supervised classifiers

notes: Correct goodput counts the requests scheduled within the 120-second arrival window whose correct label came back within that request's own SLO, divided by 120 seconds; a timely answer may complete just after the window ends. Rejected and late requests stay in the offered base. It is measured from returned labels.
The 99% rule asks every repeat to answer at least 99% of offered requests within the SLO. Passing rates are tested points; nothing between them was measured.
The three deployments use different GPU memory shares (0.40, 0.50, 0.90 in total), so differences describe these fixed deployments and do not isolate model size, architecture or co-residency.
Quality is retrospective on the ANLI test already scored in V3. Three repeats describe serving variability; repeated requests are not new independent quality samples.
